articles.title: Champions Cup: Munster beat Racing 92 on emotional day of Anthony Foley tributes as Leinster, Glasgow Warriors win big; Saracens, Bath defeated
articles.summary: A decade to the day since the rugby world learned of head coach Anthony Foley’s death at the age of 42, Munster marked the poignant anniversary with a stirring 33-25 Champions Cup victory over Racing 92.
articles.body:
Munster beat Racing 92 on an emotional anniversary, a decade to the day since their fixture was postponed following the death of coach Anthony Foley in Paris; elsewhere, Leinster and Glasgow Warriors recorded emphatic wins, while Saracens and Bath suffered damaging defeats

A decade to the day since the rugby world learned of head coach Anthony Foley’s death at the age of 42, Munster marked the poignant anniversary with a stirring 33-25 Champions Cup victory over Racing 92.

The night of Friday October 16, 2016 saw Foley pass away in his sleep the night before Munster were due to face Racing in Paris, with their fixture 10 years on staged at Páirc Uí Chaoimh in Cork.

Munster crossed for five tries in a hard-fought contest, with No 8 Brian Gleeson, wearing 24 as Foley's retired No 8 was once again taken out of circulation, joined on the scoresheet by wing Shay McCarthy, lock Tadhg Beirne, replacement Fineen Wycherley and scrum-half Craig Casey.

Racing responded with three tries of their own through wing Wilfried Hulleu, replacement scrum-half Maxime Machenaud and full-back Geronimo Prisciantelli, denying Munster a bonus-point victory. Under the tournament's new rules, teams must score at least three more tries than their opponents to secure the full five points.

The match came a day after the shocking death of Lions second row Hyron Andrews in France ahead of a Champions Cup fixture in La Rochelle. Emotional tributes were paid to both Andrews and Foley before kick-off.

Glasgow, Leinster post big opening away-day victories | Saracens lose at Connacht

Elsewhere , Glasgow Warriors extended their unbeaten start to the new season by pulling away to claim an impressive 47-27 win at Sale Sharks.

Glasgow's winning score might have looked convincing but they only secured victory in the final 20 minutes after Rekeiti Ma'asi-White had temporarily reduced Sale's deficit to four.

The game looked in the balance until late tries from Rory Darge, Ollie Smith and debutant Otavio Tuipulotu helped Glasgow pull away and wrap up a precious bonus-point win.

Leinster made a flying start to their campaign with an emphatic 48-23 victory away to Clermont Auvergne. Tadhg Furlong, Dan Sheehan (two), Sam Prendergast, Jack Conan and Tommy O'Brien all crossed the line, while a penalty try completed a dominant seven-try display.

Connacht pulled off a stunning 45-36 victory over Saracens in Galway, scoring tries through Cian Prendergast (two), Cathal Forde, Shamus Hurley-Langton, Ciaran Frawley (two) and Caolin Blade.

Bath also endured an evening to forget as they were dispatched at home by Montpellier 32-14 at the Rec in a shock result.

Lions face La Rochelle a day after death of team-mate Andrews

Players stood in silence, with some visibly emotional, as La Rochelle and the Johannesburg-based Lions paid tribute to South African lock Hyron Andrews before Saturday's Champions Cup clash. The 31-year-old died in France on Friday, on the eve of the fixture.

Andrews' No 5 jersey was laid on the pitch as his full name, Hyron Diego Andrews, appeared on the stadium's big screen. Several Lions players were visibly tearful, with team-mates embracing one another and others standing with their heads tilted back and eyes closed during the emotional tribute.

La Rochelle went on to claim a 31-14 victory, with tries from Tevita Ofa (17), Oscar Jegou (30), Davit Niniashvili (39), Tolu Latu (61) and Avakuki Niusalelekitoga (76).

articles.title: England thumped 30-12 by Tonga in Rugby League World Cup opener as Pacific Islanders claim stunning win
articles.summary: England were handed a Rugby League World Cup reality check after a 30-12 thumping by Tonga in their tournament opener.
articles.body:
England beaten 30-12 by Tonga in Rugby League World Cup opener; England trailed 10-0 at half-time after Stefano Utoikamanu try and three goals from Isaiya Katoa; AJ Brimson and Dom Young scored second-half tries but Haumole Olakau'atu double and Tolutau Koula try condemns England to defeat

England were handed a Rugby League World Cup reality check after a 30-12 thumping by Tonga in their tournament opener.

Brian McDermott's reign as England head coach got off to a dismal start as Isaiya Katoa inspired Tonga to a famous victory in Perth.

Half-back Katoa provided the precision behind Tonga's powerful forward pack. He proved the difference between the teams during a physical first half, creating a try for Stefano Utoikamanu and kicking three goals to give Tonga a 10-0 half-time lead.

England had their moments in attack despite a scoreless first half and AJ Brimson got them back into the contest with a well-worked score but two Tonga tries in three minutes, followed by another Katoa penalty, left them trailing 24-6 with 19 minutes remaining.

Dom Young's 63rd-minute try gave England hope but Haumole Olakau'atu's second try, again created by Katoa, condemned them to a chastening defeat.

England are back in Perth next Saturday where they will be expected to defeat France, but there will be plenty to ponder before then.

Their struggles under the high ball will be a concern for McDermott, with Zach Eckersley constantly targeted by Katoa during a blood-and-thunder first half.

England did enjoy plenty of possession and territory during the opening period, with George Williams and Hugo Savala both denied just shy of the tryline, but they were living on the edge at the other end and were carved open on 24 minutes.

Katoa, who lost half-back partner Latu Fainu to injury early on, received the ball in space and drew in two defenders before putting Utoikamanu through a gap to break the deadlock.

Katoa converted and slotted another kick two minutes later after Harry Smith obstructed the ever-dangerous Dallin Watene-Zelezniak.

Savala was again denied by a huge hit from Jojo Fifita while Herbie Farnworth was caught high as he charged for the line. England failed to capitalise from the penalty and things got worse for Farnworth when he was pinged for tripping Watene-Zelezniak as he again chased a Katoa kick on top of Eckersley.

Katoa's penalty made it 10-0 at the break.

England needed an early response after the restart and they got just that as another strong run from Young saw Williams and Savala put Brimson away, with Savala converting to cut arrears to four.

But they shipped a second try when Olakau'atu poked a toe at Katoa's blocked grubber, the ball ricocheting back into the path of the second rower, and Tolutau Koula bagged a third three minutes later after an inch-perfect grubber from ex-Huddersfield Giant Tui Lolohea.

Katoa converted from the touchline and added a penalty to make it 24-6, only for England to immediately hit back as Williams and Savala again combined to tee up Young.

However, any hopes of a comeback were quickly quashed as more magic from Katoa created a second try for Olakau'atu.

England are left requiring wins against France and Papua New Guinea in their remaining pool games, plus a favour or two elsewhere, if they are to reach the knockout stages.

England must regroup ahead of facing France in Perth next Saturday, kick-off 7.35am (UK and Ireland time).

articles.title: Scarlets 47-14 Newcastle Red Bulls: Wales fly-half Sam Costelow injured in Challenge Cup win
articles.summary: Scarlets hammer Newcastle but fly-half Sam Costelow gives Wales coach Steve Tandy an injury concern.
articles.body:
Tries: Costelow, Anderson, J Williams, G Davies, Mee, Page 2 Cons: Costelow 2, Hawkins 4

Tries: Spencer, Leatherbarrow Con: Hodge 2

Scarlets cantered to a seven-try bonus-point European Challenge Cup win against Newcastle Red Bulls but fly-half Sam Costelow has given Wales coach Steve Tandy an injury concern.

Costelow scored the opening try only to limp off with a hamstring problem later in the first half, just three days before Tandy names his squad for next month's Autumn Nations Championship campaign.

Wales hopeful Macs Page scored two tries on his 50th appearance while number eight Fletcher Anderson, centre Johnny Williams, scrum-half Gareth Davies and wing Ellis Mee also crossed as Scarlets began their European campaign in style.

It was an unsuccessful return to Llanelli for former Scarlets and Wales fly-half Stephen Jones, now a Newcastle assistant coach, who locked horns with his former half-back partner Dwayne Peel.

Newcastle responded with late tries from Oliver Spencer and Ollie Leatherbarrow as they suffered a fourth successive defeat following three losses in the Prem.

Friends reunited as Scarlets soar in first half

In front of a crowd of 5,629, Anderson and Davies, who impressed as replacements in the 27-26 win against Benetton , made their first starts of the season.

Newcastle fielded a much-changed side as they gave debuts to wing Brandon Jackson and Argentina prop Francisco Moreno, while 18-year-old Scottish fly-half Jake Dalziel started.

Full-back Blair Murray provided the first inspirational moment with a 60-metre counter-attacking run but the move came to nothing.

Costelow opened the scoring with an opportunistic individual try, gliding through the heart of the Newcastle defence.

Scrum-half Davies, who has been tipped for a Wales recall if he decides to reverse his international retirement , provided the catalyst for the second score when his clever cross-field kick was gathered by Mee who was dragged down just short of the line before Anderson charged over.

A well-worked third try saw lock Alex Groves power through the visitors' defence before providing the try-scoring pass to centre Williams.

Scarlets' indiscipline, with infringements including backchat to the referee and kicking the ball away, provided Newcastle with an attacking platform but they could not capitalise.

Joe Hawkins came on for Costelow and converted the fourth try scored by Davies, following a fine Mee break.

Plumtree returns as hosts make numbers tells

The hosts led 26-0 at half-time and had the luxury of bringing on Wales back row Taine Plumtree to make his first appearance of the season after recovering from shoulder surgery.

Captain Josh Macleod continued his impressive start to the season as he repeatedly demonstrated his ability to turnover possession to put his side on the front foot.

Newcastle replacement prop Murray McCallum was shown a yellow card and Scarlets took advantage of the extra player by working the ball to Mee in the right corner.

Scarlets were rampant and scored straight from the restart after breaks from Anderson and centre Joe Roberts paved the way for Page to collect a grubber kick and sprint over unopposed.

A second for Page soon followed as he followed up Mee's well-measured inside kick before Newcastle finally responded with an opportunist effort from replacement Spencer before Leatherbarrow completed the scoring.

With only one game in the first European block before the next round of matches in December, Scarlets face a tough United Rugby Championship (URC) double-header in South Africa against Stormers and Bulls, while Newcastle return to action in the Prem when they host Sale next Saturday.

articles.title: Mundial 2035: Una final en el Camp Nou, cuestión de aforo
articles.standfirst: Es la de mayor tamaño entre las presuntas sedes mundialistas
articles.summary: Es la de mayor tamaño entre las presuntas sedes mundialistas
articles.body: La elaboración de la candidatura española al Mundial de rugby masculino 2035 -y del femenino 2037- sigue su curso. La reciente presentación de 'Bridge the World', las bases de la candidatura española se ha visto seguida por interpretaciones, una de las cuales señala la designación del Camp Nou como sede de una hipotética final. La candidatura se basa, como señaló MARCA en su momento, en la situación geográfica española, apta para atraer a gran cantidad de público procedente del Reino Unido, Francia e Italia, los países del VI Naciones; la calidad de sus infraestructuras, reflejada en la condición de ser uno de los principales destinos turísticos del mundo; un apoyo institucional transversal y a largo plazo, basado en la consideración del evento como una cuestión de Estado, y en la calidad de los estadios como elemento central de la infraestructura. 'Bridge The World' no cita expresamente estadios, pero sí ciudades sede, con lo cual se colige que Camp Nou, Bernabéu, Metropolitano, La Cartuja, Mestalla, La Rosaleda y otros figurarían entre los estadios mundialistas. En este sentido, no es oficial la consideración del Camp Nou como sede de la final pero alude a su condición de ser el mayor de los estadios que serían sede mundialista, lo que es una condición que interesa a World Rugby. Todos los estadios de la candidatura habrán sido objeto de remodelaciones y actualizaciones para el Mundial de Fútbol 2030. Todas las sedes -como sucede con el resto de candidaturas, la sudamericana y la probable de Japón- son normalmente empleados para el fútbol, lo que convierte a la Liga de Fútbol Profesional en uno de los elementos fundamentales de la candidatura. El organismo ya le ha dado su apoyo y se ha comprometido a, en su caso, adaptar los calendarios -el Mundial tendría lugar en el principio del otoño- para la celebración de lo que es el tercer evento más importante del deporte, tras los Juegos Olímpicos y el Mundial de Fútbol. El Camp Nou cuenta, por otra parte, con su propia tradición rugbística. En 2016 congregó a 99.124 espectadores en la final del 'Top 14' francés entre Racing Metro y Toulouse. Y en los planes franceses está volver al estadio blaugrana en 2028.

articles.title: Champions Cup: Gloucester 36-36 Bordeaux Begles - thrilling draw to start 2026-27 competition
articles.summary: Gloucester and holders Bordeaux Begles begin this season's Champions Cup with a thrilling 36-36 draw at Kingsholm.
articles.body:
Tries: Clark, Llewellyn, Barton, Trenholm 2 Cons: Barton 4 Pens Barton

Tries: Page-Relo, Falatea, Uberti, Bielle-Biarrey 2 Cons: Lucu 4 Pen: Lucu

Gloucester and holders Bordeaux Begles began this season's Champions Cup with a thrilling 36-36 draw at Kingsholm.

Bordeaux, bidding to win the Champions Cup for a third successive year, had looked in danger of their first loss in the competition since a quarter-final defeat by Harlequins in April 2024.

The French side trailed 24-17 at the interval and then 36-29 when Gloucester replacement Will Trenholm crossed twice midway through the second half for the early-season Prem leaders.

But France winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey quickly replied with his second try of the game, which was converted by Maxime Lucu, and neither team was able to produce a winning moment in a gripping finale.

Before kick-off, there was a moment's silence in memory of Lions lock Hyron Andrews, who died on Friday aged 31.

Former Sale player Andrews died at the South African team's hotel a day before their Champions Cup match in La Rochelle.

The Lions will fulfil that fixture in Andrews' honour on Saturday and further tributes are planned across the opening round of Champions Cup games.

Recap: Gloucester and holders Bordeaux draw thrilling Champions Cup opener

Gloucester's three first-half tries all owed a lot to their strength at the scrum, although they twice had to come from behind to lead by seven points at the interval.

Bordeaux scrum-half Martin Page-Relo nipped clear to score the opener inside five minutes but the hosts responded well with replies from Arthur Clark and Max Llewellyn.

Sipili Falatea profited from a powerful carry by Englishman Tom Willis to level the score once more and Bordeaux captain Lucu kicked the visitors in front with a penalty from inside his own half.

Gloucester eventually took advantage of a prolonged spell of pressure when George Barton barged his way over from close range and the full-back kicked a penalty to close out the first half, adding to his three earlier conversions.

Bielle-Biarrey, who had been kept quiet in the first 40 minutes, sent fellow winger Pablo Uberti over in the corner before grabbing his first try to restore Bordeaux's lead in a see-saw Pool Three encounter.

Trenholm's quickfire double and Bielle-Biarrey's second completed the scoring, taking both sides to five tries for the evening, and they both had chances for points in the closing stages.

Gloucester elected to kick a penalty to touch rather than go for the posts and lost possession, while Bordeaux could not capitalise on a scrum in Gloucester territory late on.

articles.title: Challenge Cup: Melvyn Jaminet stars as Toulon beat Edinburgh
articles.summary: Edinburgh suffer their first defeat of the season as they go down to Toulon in their European Challenge Cup opener.
articles.body:
Tries: Ashman, Gwynn Cons: Grayson 2 Pens: Grayson

Tries: Jaminet 2, Tuicuvu Cons: Jaminet 3 Pens: Jaminet 2

Edinburgh suffered their first defeat of the season as they went down to Toulon in their European Challenge Cup opener.

Melvyn Jaminet inspired the French side to victory, scoring two tries and contributing 22 points in a superb individual display.

The France full-back kicked two penalties, the second from well inside his own half, to give the visitors a 6-0 lead.

Edinburgh engineered some good openings but were unable to break through as they were met with some fierce French goal-line defence.

James Grayson kicked a penalty to reduce the gap to three points heading into the break.

Toulon struck early in the second half when Edinburgh were turned over in the French 22. The ball was spun wide to Jaminet who sprinted free, chipped ahead and gathered to go over for a wonderful score.

The home side hit back almost immediately with a cleverly worked set-piece. Ewan Ashman threw to Tom Currie coming through the middle of the lineout. He then set Ashman free to race up the touchline and over the line to make it a three-point game once again.

A powerful Toulon maul drove them to the brink of the Edinburgh line before Scotland scrum-half Ben White slipped a lovely little delayed pass to Seta Tuicuvu to crash over.

At 20-10 down, the game looked to be slipping away, but Edinburgh responded again when Currie's tackle caused Toulon fly-half Matteo Garcia to fumble in midfield and replacement Geordie Gwynn scooped up and raced free to go in under the posts.

Toulon were undeterred, and another rolling maul laid the platform for Jeremy Sinzelle to slip in Jaminet for his second try of the night to all-but end Edinburgh's resistance.

articles.title: Dragons 29-14 Perpignan - Welsh side win Challenge Cup opener
articles.summary: Dragons turn a half-time deficit around to beat Perpignan in their Challenge Cup opener at Rodney Parade.
articles.body:
Tries: Rosser, Owen, Tuitavuki, Paea Cons: De Beer 3 Pen: De Beer

Dragons started their Challenge Cup campaign with a hard-fought win against Perpignan at Rodney Parade.

Filo Tiatia's side, semi-finalists in 2025-26, ran in four tries in Newport to edge a scrappy opener, but did not claim a bonus point after this season's change in rules.

Perpignan led 7-5 after a drab first half by responding to Jared Rosser's opener with a try from Jules Coulon.

Dragons backs Aneurin Owen and Anzelo Tuitavuki scored either side of a powerful effort by Posolo Tuilagi to secure victory against their French opponents, with Fetuli Paea adding a flourish in the closing stages.

Five tries would have been needed for a bonus due to Perpignan, who are yet to win away from their Stade Aime Giral home this season, scoring twice.

Dragons suffer Woodman bicep injury blow

Dragons trio continuing Gwent's Tongan tradition

Dragons, with a number of influential players either injured or given a breather before a derby at Ospreys, failed to perform as well as they have at the start of the United Rugby Championship (URC).

Nonetheless, they got the job done to put themselves in a strong position for the last 16 with a pair of fixtures to come in Wales.

In December they face South Africa's Cheetahs at the redeveloped St Helen's in Swansea before January fixtures against Bayonne in Newport and Ulster in Belfast.

The win did come at a cost, with loose-head props Rhodri and Wyn Jones going off a week after Argentina international Rodrigo Martinez was injured in defeat by Ospreys.

Dragons made a fast start for Rosser to go over down the left in the fifth minute from a multi-phase attack - moving the wing joint second with Ashton Hewitt on the club's all-time try chart with 37, six behind Aled Brew - but failed to build on the opener.

Perpignan grew into the game, and their pressure eventually told when flanker Coulon went over from close range approaching the half hour, with full-back Tristan Tedder converting for a 7-5 lead.

The French side dominated possession, territory and chances, and would have been disappointed to only hold a two-point advantage after a low-quality half.

Jac Lloyd had a try chalked off for crossing, and it was Dragons' turn to waste chances in the 22 after turning down shots at goal.

The driving line-out that has been a potent weapon in the URC was going nowhere, but quick ball off the top did the trick after 55 minutes, centre Owen exploiting weak defence.

The lead was taken away when lock Posolo Tuilagi, whose uncle Anitelea played for Dragons, crashed over, only for Tinus de Beer to kick a penalty to make it 15-14 with quarter of an hour to go.

Dragons finally had breathing space thanks to the South African's tricky conversion of a close-range finish from Tonga wing Tuitavuki.

He was followed over in the closing stages by compatriot Fetuli Paea, the centre's first for the club, but they were unable to get another try for a bonus.

"The most pleasing part was guys just finding a way and making it happen. We chased the game to get that extra bonus but didn't quite get there.

"There are still areas to grow but we spoke about our physicality from the week before [against Ospreys] and the boys were outstanding on both sides of the ball. I am really proud of the group."

articles.title: Champions Cup: Gloucester claim thrilling draw against holders Bordeaux
articles.summary: Will Trenholm scores a brace of tries as Gloucester fall just short of beating Champions Cup holders Bordeaux in a thrilling 36-36 draw; Edinburgh suffered a 27-17 defeat against Toulon in their Challenge Cup opener
articles.body:
George Skivington's team pushed the French outfit all the way during a pulsating European tie at Kingsholm Stadium.

Gloucester held a 24-17 lead at half-time before Trenholm crashed over twice, but a double by Louis Bielle-Biarrey salvaged a share of the spoils for visiting Bordeaux.

Bordeaux made a fast start, with Martin Page-Relo able to open the scoring in the fourth minute, but Arthur Clark produced an instant reply for Gloucester.

Efforts by Max Llewellyn and George Barton, either side of Sipili Falatea's try, earned the hosts a slender seven-point advantage at the break thanks to three successful conversions by Barton.

Pablo Uberti levelled for Bordeaux six minutes into the second period before quick-fire tries by Trenholm had Kingsholm rocking, but Bielle-Biarry levelled in the 62nd minute and despite plenty of territory, neither side could find a winning score.

Edinburgh beaten by Toulon in Challenge Cup opener

Edinburgh suffered a 27-17 defeat against Toulon in their Challenge Cup opener as Malvyn Jaminet scored 22 points for the French visitors.

Defences were on top in the first half at the Hive Stadium, with two Jaminet penalties to one from James Grayson giving Toulon a 6-3 lead at the break.

Jaminet extended that advantage three minutes into the second half, collecting his own kick before converting his try.

Scotland hooker Ewan Ashman hit back immediately for Edinburgh, with Grayson adding the conversion, but Fiji international Seta Tuicuvu soon barged over and Jaminet again added the extras.

Edinburgh refused to go away, with replacement Geordie Gwynn scoring with his first touch before Grayson converted to keep the hosts in contention.

But Toulon had the final say. Baptiste Serin set up Jaminet for another converted try, while Piers O'Conor's yellow card for direct contact with Jeremy Sinzelle's head compounded Edinburgh's misery and sealed their fate.

articles.title: Women's Rugby League World Cup: England crush debutants Wales in Perth
articles.summary: England scored seven tries before the break, and 13 in total on their way to a comprehensive victory over Wales in their Group A opener.
articles.body:
Tries : Boyd 3, Davies 3, Brown 2, Rowe 2, Wilson, Dodd, Strange Goals : Rowe 9

For a moment, when Paige Travis bundled over the line to spark wild celebrations, Wales were in dreamland.

On their Women's World Cup debut, they had scored against England, taking advantage of multiple English errors to deservedly pull level inside the opening 10 minutes.

Wales could dream of causing a major upset. By half-time, though, England had thoroughly disabused Wales of that notion.

The shock of conceding against a team they had scored 114 points against without reply in two previous meetings brought renewed focus to Stu Barrow's England team, who are aiming to reach a World Cup final for the first time.

They scored seven tries before the break and 13 in total on their way to a comprehensive 70-6 victory in Perth in their Group A opener.

Wing Anna Davies and debutant Connie Boyd scored hat-tricks in Perth, while Izzy Rowe scored two tries and kicked nine conversions for 26 points - equalling the record for the most points by an individual England player in a Women's World Cup match.

Women's Rugby League World Cup: England score 70 in emphatic win over Wales

While Wales provided threat going forwards, in defence they provided little resistance as England's powerful attack pierced through with frightening ease.

A slick move after three minutes resulted in Amelia Brown scoring the England opener, before Wales got their time in the sun.

A series of England errors allowed Wales to apply pressure, and they deservedly scored through Travis - who represented England at the World Cup four years ago.

The shock concession brought England focus, and a well-constructed move ended in Georgia Wilson scoring in the corner.

Hollie-Mae Dodd's drive and offload ended in Boyd scoring her first, before Dodd deservedly got on the scoresheet herself, following up after Fran Goldthorp was held up on the line.

On 27 minutes, a quick move of the ball through hands to the left allowed Boyd to power through, before Davies ran more than half the length of the field to score under the posts.

Rowe got a try of her own before the interval, making it 40-6 at half-time.

The heavy scoring continued after the break.

Another debutant, Jasmin Strange - one of two heritage players not born in England - also bagged her first try, before Rowe rolled over her second.

The match was summed up by England's 10th try, when a promising Wales attack involved a chipped kick to the corner, but the bounce went kindly for Brown behind her own try line.

Brown raced 109 metres up to the other end to score one of the longest-range tries in women's rugby league history, and thoroughly demoralise Wales.

Boyd and Davies wrapped it up with three tries in the final five minutes.

When England and Wales met for the first time, at Headingley in 2024, England won 82-0 in a match which could be best described as women against girls.

Two years down the line, they took to the field as teams who had each earned their spot on the World Cup stage - but England showed why they remain by far the more dominant force.

It was always going to be a difficult Rugby League World Cup debut for Wales, who had lost their previous two games against England by a combined score of 144-0.

Captain Bethan Dainton had said in the build-up to the tournament they wanted to remain competitive despite only having played 13 international games as a nation.

And for the opening quarter of an hour in Perth they were exactly that, and will have been delighted when Paige Travis crossed for Wales' first ever Rugby League World Cup try.

But the intensity soon caught up with Wales, who by the half-hour mark looked exhausted compared to their opponents, who never showed signs of stopping.

And as the game wore on, the gulf between the two sides became more evident, with England running in three tries in the final minutes to put an exclamation point on their win.

But head coach Tom Brindle will take positives from the game, and in the long run Wales will benefit for the experience of competing at a World Cup despite the heavy defeats they will encounter along the way.

Next up for Wales is Samoa on Friday, a game which on paper serves as their best chance at picking up a result, having also been drawn in Pool A alongside reigning world champions Australia.

It's sometimes easy to pick halves for player of the match because they have so many touches of the ball, but Rowe has put women's rugby league on notice with a display that shows her immense talent.

She combined brilliantly with her back-rower Jasmin Strange on numerous occasions and scored two tries of her own - linking up well with Georgia Roche and then Jenna Foubister when she came on.

Georgia Wilson, Hollie-Mae Dodd, Amelia Brown and Connie Boyd also put their hands up, but Rowe's control was such that she just nudges it.

articles.title: Men's Rugby League World Cup: England stunned by Tonga in opener
articles.summary: England 's men fall to defeat in their Rugby League World Cup opener as Tonga take their chances in Perth.
articles.body:
Tries : Olakau'atu 2, Utoikamanu, Koula Goals : Katoa 3 Penalties : Katoa 4

Four years ago, England were left shocked and shattered by Samoa in the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals.

Now in 2026, Tonga - another Pacific island nation - have done the same with a victory to put England's Australian campaign in immediate jeopardy.

Tonga combined classy attacking play with staunch defence, mixed with a pinch of luck - while being cheered on by a ferociously partisan crowd in Perth - to cause a major upset.

It was expected that Brian McDermott's team - ranked third in the world - would have enough to open their Group B-C campaign with victory over opponents ranked fifth.

But they will now have to pick themselves up for coming group games against France and Papua New Guinea to try to secure a top-two finish in the combined six-team group table and secure a semi-final spot.

Australia, Papua New Guinea, New Zealand

Listen to live commentary on every men's match, and key women's matches - with coverage on BBC Radio 5 Live, BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra, BBC Sounds and the BBC Sport website and app

England's day came apart amid seemingly endless mistakes, wastefulness and a few dodgy refereeing decisions.

Arguably the turning point came on 22 minutes, when England got to within a few yards of the opposition line but Victor Radley knocked on after an absolute boneshaker from Tonga captain Jason Taumalolo.

The ball was turned over, and the Tongans scored two minutes later. Stefano Utoikamanu streaked through after Isaiya Katoa's superb inside pass cut out George Williams and Kai Pearce-Paul, to the delight of the massed Tongan fans in Perth.

For England, it seemed as if the universe was against them.

The impressive Katoa converted two penalties given following debatable calls. First, Harry Smith was penalised for obstruction when Dallin Watene-Zelezniak ran into him. Then, Herbie Farnworth conceded a sloppy penalty on the verge of half-time when accidentally tripping Watene-Zelezniak off the ball.

England badly needed half-time, and they came out refreshed.

Their first flowing move of the home game led to a try for full-back AJ Brimson after being set up by a sensational driving run from Young, holding off two tacklers over 20 metres.

Waves of England attacks began to crash on the Tongan defence, but Tonga stood firm and benefited from a moment of fortune as Haumole Olakau'atu pounced after his sketchy first grubber kick was kicked on behind the England line.

And with England wobbling, Tonga landed a one-two punch when Tolutau Koula drove over the line.

Young went over in the corner to give England false hope, but in front of their delirious fans Tonga scored their fourth try as Katoa's grubber kick exploited defensive gaps for Olakau'atu to touch down.

In the day's other men's game - also in Group B-C - co-hosts Papua New Guinea defeated Lebanon 42-18.

articles.title: Canada 24-21 England: Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten run ends in Toronto
articles.summary: England's 41-match unbeaten streak ends in dramatic fashion as Shoshanah Seumanutafa's late try hands Canada a thrilling 24-21 victory in Toronto.
articles.body:
Tries: Bauder, Corrigan, Menin, Seumanutafa Cons: De Goede (2)

Tries: Feaunati, Harrison, Bern Cons: Harrison (3)

England's 41-match unbeaten streak ended in dramatic fashion as Shoshanah Seumanutafa's late try handed Canada a thrilling 24-21 victory in Toronto.

Canada, who previously snapped England's 39-match winning run with a 26-26 draw in Exeter in September, are the first team to defeat the Red Roses since November 2022, when they lost to New Zealand in the World Cup final.

Playing in front of 18,621 fans, a record for a standalone women's fixture in North America, the result also marks England's first defeat by Canada since 2016 and their first against their hosts on Canadian soil, having won their previous 11 away matches.

Canada's Savannah Bauder took advantage of Zoe Harrison's yellow card to open the scoring in the 15th minute, but it was England who took a 14-5 half-time lead, hitting back late in the first half through Maddie Feaunati and Harrison, with Laetitia Royer in the sin-bin for the hosts.

Sarah Bern cancelled out a stylish solo try from the hosts' Alysha Corrigan early in the second half to preserve England's nine-point lead before Canada's DaLeaka Menin crashed over for a converted score just after the hour mark to set up a tense finale.

Three minutes from time, Canada mounted an attack from halfway after a fumble put Harrison's clearing kick under pressure, and replacement Seumanutafa charged down the left wing to complete the comeback.

"We're not driven by outcome. We're disappointed by the result but there was some very good things in our performance. So we'll stick to our processes," said England head coach John Mitchell, following his first defeat since being appointed in late 2023.

"I guess [the loss] frees us up and allows us to find more. I know this group has got more in them. Sometimes it requires the context that we've just received to dig deeper and find something more."

The two sides will renew their rivalry in Ottawa on Friday, 23 October (in the early hours of Saturday on UK time) before England conclude their 2026 WXV Global Series against the USA in New Jersey on Friday, 30 October (21:15 GMT).

'We're still world champions, we're still number one'

This result has been coming for England, who showcased vulnerability in their three WXV Global Series home matches in September.

Against Australia, the world champions trailed at half-time for the first time since 2020 before roaring back with seven second-half tries for a 48-15 win. The following week, Canada held them to a draw in Exeter while a nail-biting 26-19 win over New Zealand at Twickenham was secured with the clock in the red.

This time, Canada's defensive resilience in the face of repeated attacks kept the world champions off the scoreboard until the 32nd minute, but England also lacked a clinical touch in their opponents' 22, with multiple opportunities going begging. Notably, Claudia Moloney-MacDonald had an early try chalked off for a knock-on in the grounding.

In defence, multiple penalties afforded Canada the freedom to form free-flowing attacks while it was an individual handling error when delivering the ball to fly-half Harrison which gave the hosts field position to score their match-winning try.

The result places England in uncharted territory, with several players in the squad never having tasted defeat on the international stage - winger Jess Breach was unbeaten in her previous 59 caps.

But for captain Meg Jones, it is no time to panic. England are "still world champions" and her message is simple: "Stick together, look out for each other, and we go again."

She added: "We've got to remember, there's a target on our back continuously. Everyone's got that underdog mentality, that underdog fight.

"We've got to be in a position now where we've got to be the quickest to respond. That's the nature of the game.

"What an amazing achievement for us as a group. I think they will go down in history as one of the best sporting teams.

"We're still world champions, we're still number one, and we'll still keep pushing to be the best we possibly can."

In September, Canada captain Sophie de Goede confessed she still has sleepless nights about her side's World Cup final defeat by England in 2025.

Even after ending the Red Roses' winning run in Exeter, she was frustrated at being denied the opportunity to go for the win, although reluctantly conceding that head coach Kevin Rouet's call to kick the ball dead was the sensible one.

After a historic performance in Toronto, where De Goede's side showcased "the DNA of our team" and "found a way to win", sleep might once again be hard to come by – albeit for far happier reasons.

"It's a little bit more than just the score at the end because we won on so many levels," added scrum-half Justine Pelletier. "Off the field, the crowd, being home. That win at the end on the pitch was just the cherry on [top].

"It was good to beat England but I think for a few years now, we knew that we could beat them. It was just a matter of time and a matter of putting every detail together."

articles.title: WXV Global Series: England stunned by a late rally from Canada as Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten run ends with 24-21 loss
articles.summary: Canada’s women snapped world champion England’s 41-match unbeaten run with a 24-21 victory in Toronto on Friday
articles.body:
Shoshanah Seumanutafa came off the bench to score the match-winning try in the 77th minute to hand England their first defeat since the 2022 World Cup final.

Following a draw in their previous clash last month in Exeter , Canada looked up for the challenge early as they opened the scoring through Savannah Bauder in the 15th minute.

Quickfire tries to Maddie Feaunati and Zoe Harrison just before half-time put England ahead 14-5 at the break.

The points kept flowing as both teams crossed just after play resumed, but DaLeaka Menin's 63rd-minute try kept the door open for Canada.

A raucous home crowd exploded for Seumanutafa's match-winner shortly after, with Canada able to hold on from there and quell England's historic run.

Speaking after the match, England's head coach John Mitchell said he was focused on taking what positives he could out of the loss.

He said: "We're not driven by outcome. We're disappointed by the result but there was some very good things in our performance tonight. So we'll stick to our processes.

"I guess (the loss) frees us up and allows us all to find more.

"I know this group has got more in them but sometimes it requires the context that we've just received to dig deeper and find something more.

"Maybe everyone in the group can probably review their 'why's and re-establish those as well because I'm sure they're changing and evolving as they experience what we're going through."

The opener of a two-game Rugby Rematch Tour between the growing rivals drew an electric crowd to BMO Field as Canada returned to home soil for the first time since ​finishing runner-up to the Red Roses at last year's World Cup.

"I think it's a ⁠little bit more than just the score at ⁠the end because we won on so many levels today," Canada's Justine Pelletier said.

"Off the field, just the crowd, being home, and there's so much ‌going on around. And I think that win at the end on the pitch was just the cherry on (top).

"It was good to beat England, but I think for a few years now we knew ⁠that we could beat them. It was just a matter of time ​and a matter of putting every detail together."

"The bit we always remember is we're at the ​top, and when you're at the top, people want to bring you down as quick as ⁠they can," England captain Megan Jones said, adding that the team take "huge pride" in their unbeaten run.

Canada's last win over England came in 2016 at the Women's Rugby Super Series.

Mitchell's side will face Canada again next Saturday in Ottawa before completing the away leg of their Global Series fixtures against the USA in New Jersey on October 30.

Scotland Women fell to an eighth consecutive defeat as a rampant Australia ran in five tries in a dominant first half, paving the way for a 56-12 victory in Sydney.

Desiree Miller scored 42 consecutive points, and with her opening try she became the first Wallaroo to have scored 20 Test tries.

The teams will play again in Canberra on Friday.

articles.title: England 70-6 Wales: Connie Boyd and Anna Davies hat-tricks propel Lionesses to dominant opening Women's Rugby League World Cup win
articles.summary: England record a dominant 70-6 win over Wales in their opening match of the Women's Rugby League World Cup; Former Lioness Paige Travis secured Wales' first ever try at the tournament; England take on a vaunted Australia side on October 25, with Wales facing Samoa the day before
articles.body:
The Lionesses took the lead just four minutes into the game and never let up, scoring 13 tries in a sensational victory against a weak Welsh side that lacked quality in both attack and defence.

Boyd, Davies, and Isabel Rowe stood out, with the latter ending the match with a 26-point haul after scoring two tries and recording nine successful conversion attempts.

The win gives Stuart Barrow's side a valuable platform in the pool stage ahead of their next match against a vaunted Australia side next Saturday, while Wales have work to do against Samoa to stand any chance of progressing.

England produce complete performance to dominate in tournament opener

Some deft attacking play from England early on set up Amelia Brown to bundle over after just four minutes, but Wales took advantage of some sloppy handling and an eventual penalty that allowed former England international Paige Travis to level the scores with Wales' first World Cup try.

Their parity, though, was short-lived, with Megan Williams, Jasmin Strange, and Isabel Rowe linking up neatly to give centre Georgia Wilson a clear path to the tryline, before Hollie-Mae Dodd's sharp offload allowed Connie Boyd to score on debut just three minutes later, giving England a 10-point lead after 24 minutes.

Wales struggled to contain England's rapid tempo from then on, with Dodd, Boyd's second of the day, a stunning solo effort from Anna Davies, and Rowe's try on the stroke of half-time adding 24 points - thanks in no small part to Rowe's excellent goal-kicking - to the scoreline to give England a seemingly unassailable 40-6 at the break.

The second half began in a similar fashion, with debutant Strange bundling over just after the restart, before Rowe crossed to take her side to a mammoth total of 50 points.

Winger Brown scored the try of the day minutes afterwards with a sensational run down the wing after receiving a kick behind her own tryline.

Interchange Jenna Foubister then produced a brilliant offload to facilitate Boyd's hat-trick six minutes from time, with Davies going over twice in the final minutes to complete her treble and put the cherry on top of a brilliant victory to begin her side's World Cup campaign.

England captain Jodie Cunningham, speaking on Premier Sports:

"It feels good. We knew Wales were going to come out really passionate, really energetic, and those first 10-15 minutes were tough, but proud of the girls the way they stuck into it.

"[Amelia Brown] has got some pace doesn't she!

"She does that for fun in the Super League and I'm glad to see her do it in an England shirt.

"[Rowe] is so young but so mature in the way she plays. She takes us around the field, she's so calm on the ball, and her kicking game was outstanding as well. Another one who's got a really bright future.

"Job one done. We'll regroup, see where we can improve - we've got a huge game next week."

Dainton: Scoreline didn't reflect the game

Wales captain Bethan Dainton, speaking on Premier Sports:

"So proud of the girls despite the scoreline. I don't think it reflected the game - we were in the game for quite a bit of it.

"It was just some lapses in concentration that let England get on the front foot."

articles.title: Eight-try Australia send Scotland to eighth straight defeat
articles.summary: Scotland suffer a chastening eight-try defeat by Australia in their WXV Global Series match in Sydney.
articles.body:
Tries: Merlo, Stewart, Miller (2), Whitaker (2), Ellis, Karpani Cons: Wood (6), Moleka (2)

Scotland suffered a chastening eight-try defeat by Australia in their WXV Global Series match in Sydney.

It was the visitors' eighth straight defeat, four of them in the new competition, having lost to Canada, New Zealand and the Aussies in their home ties.

Australia have two victories, both against the Scots, after losing to England and France, their 30-10 win in Edinburgh having lifted them above their hosts in the world rankings.

As they sought revenge, the Scots, under caretaker head coach Dave Butcher, lost Sarah Bonar to illness shortly before kick-off and the Harlequins lock was replaced with Bristol Bears' Hollie Cunningham.

But they started brightly, with Katie Buchanan collecting the ball on the wing, beating a defender and sprinting over the line to give them a fifth-minute lead in her first international start.

Australia, though, responded with five tries by half-time.

England's 41-match unbeaten run ended by Canada

The Scots held on to the lead until the 17th-minute, when hooker Brittany Merlo went over to draw the hosts level and wing Maya Stewart added another six minutes later, with Samantha Wood converting both.

Australia took complete control after centre Meryl Smith was sent to the sin-bin and Desiree Miller, Amelia Whitaker and Ellis all scored to give the hosts a commanding 35-5 lead at the break.

Miller crossed for her second two minutes after the restart, but the Scots did manage a reply soon after as captain Rachel Malcolm would not be denied close to the line and Helen Nelson added the conversion.

Scotland managed to hold out for close to another 20 minutes before Whitaker broke clear to score her second try with 15 minutes remaining.

The hosts completed the scoring in the closing seconds through Eva Karpani after Scotland lost second row Eva Donaldson to a yellow card.

articles.title: Bledisloe Cup: New Zealand sweep past Australia in Sydney to stretch winning streak over rivals to 13 Tests
articles.summary: All Blacks score six first-half tries to take 36-7 lead at interval as crowd of 73,399 watch Australia record three tries in 43-21 defeat; New Zealand had retained Bledisloe Cup with 50-19 victory in Auckland last week
articles.body:
With the Bledisloe Cup already ​safely in the cupboard for a 24th year after last week's 50-19 win in Auckland , New Zealand exploded out of the blocks and crushed all thoughts of an upset with six tries ​before the break at Accor Stadium, Sydney.

Despite losing Jordie Barrett to a calf injury before kick-off and another centre ‌in Quinn Tupaea early on with a concussion, the All Blacks overwhelmed the Wallabies with power, pace and precision in the opening 40 minutes.

"I'm ​really proud of the boys, the way we came out on that in that first half," said New Zealand captain Codie Taylor.

"It was a real challenge for us this week to make sure that we backed up a really ​good performance from last week, and I thought we were awesome in that first 40."

Australia showed ⁠some flashes of backline brilliance, particularly in the second ⁠half, but struggled to get hold of the ball for prolonged periods and were unable to match the accuracy or clinical finishing of the All Blacks.

In a whirlwind of ‌offloads, winger Josh Moorby, fullback Beauden Barrett, flanker Peter Lakai and replacement back Rieko Ioane all crossed in the first 26 minutes to give the visitors a quick-fire 22-0 lead.

Wallabies fly-half Declan Meredith did well to get a pass away in ‌the tackle just before the half-hour mark to send Jeremy Williams over for a try but the lock was sin-binned at the other end of the field two minutes later.

All Blacks No 8 Wallace Sititi immediately made the extra man count with his team's fifth try and Beauden Barrett added a sixth, his second, off an intercept to send New Zealand into ⁠the break with a 36-7 lead.

Moorby faked out the defence for his second five-pointer within ​three minutes of the restart before the Wallabies finally finished off a backline move ​for fullback Tom Wright to go over.

Australia were looking stronger with their replacements on the pitch, and ​Meredith almost scored a try after a scything break up the middle, then saved a try at the ⁠other end.

A clever line dropout from Wright did result in a third Australia try in the 66th minute for replacement back Filipo Daugunu that delighted the majority of the crowd of 73,399.

New Zealand were reduced to 14 men after Samisoni Taukei'aho went off injured, ⁠and went down to 13 when debutant Chay Fihaki was shown ​a yellow card but managed to hold out the Wallabies for the last few minutes.

"I'm gutted," said Wallabies ​captain Harry Wilson. "When you give a team like the All Blacks a head start it's tough, and it's not good enough for this group.

"We've got to be a lot better. It's ‌been a very disappointing series, and we're ​going to have to regroup."

The last time Australia beat New Zealand was at Brisbane in 2020 when current All Blacks coach Dave Rennie was in charge of the Wallabies. The same Sydney venue will host the teams for a Rugby World Cup pool match in a year's time.

articles.title: England thumped 30-12 by Tonga in Rugby League World Cup opener as Pacific Islanders claim stunning win
articles.summary: England beaten 30-12 by Tonga in Rugby League World Cup opener; England trailed 10-0 at half-time after Stefano Utoikamanu try and three goals from Isaiya Katoa; AJ Brimson and Dom Young scored second-half tries but Haumole Olakau'atu double and Tolutau Koula try condemns England to defeat
articles.body:
Brian McDermott's reign as England head coach got off to a dismal start as Isaiya Katoa inspired Tonga to a famous victory in Perth.

Half-back Katoa provided the precision behind Tonga's powerful forward pack. He proved the difference between the teams during a physical first half, creating a try for Stefano Utoikamanu and kicking three goals to give Tonga a 10-0 half-time lead.

England had their moments in attack despite a scoreless first half and AJ Brimson got them back into the contest with a well-worked score but two Tonga tries in three minutes, followed by another Katoa penalty, left them trailing 24-6 with 19 minutes remaining.

Dom Young's 63rd-minute try gave England hope but Haumole Olakau'atu's second try, again created by Katoa, condemned them to a chastening defeat.

England are back in Perth next Saturday where they will be expected to defeat France, but there will be plenty to ponder before then.

Their struggles under the high ball will be a concern for McDermott, with Zach Eckersley constantly targeted by Katoa during a blood-and-thunder first half.

England did enjoy plenty of possession and territory during the opening period, with George Williams and Hugo Savala both denied just shy of the tryline, but they were living on the edge at the other end and were carved open on 24 minutes.

Katoa, who lost half-back partner Latu Fainu to injury early on, received the ball in space and drew in two defenders before putting Utoikamanu through a gap to break the deadlock.

Katoa converted and slotted another kick two minutes later after Harry Smith obstructed the ever-dangerous Dallin Watene-Zelezniak.

Savala was again denied by a huge hit from Jojo Fifita while Herbie Farnworth was caught high as he charged for the line. England failed to capitalise from the penalty and things got worse for Farnworth when he was pinged for tripping Watene-Zelezniak as he again chased a Katoa kick on top of Eckersley.

Katoa's penalty made it 10-0 at the break.

England needed an early response after the restart and they got just that as another strong run from Young saw Williams and Savala put Brimson away, with Savala converting to cut arrears to four.

But they shipped a second try when Olakau'atu poked a toe at Katoa's blocked grubber, the ball ricocheting back into the path of the second rower, and Tolutau Koula bagged a third three minutes later after an inch-perfect grubber from ex-Huddersfield Giant Tui Lolohea.

Katoa converted from the touchline and added a penalty to make it 24-6, only for England to immediately hit back as Williams and Savala again combined to tee up Young.

However, any hopes of a comeback were quickly quashed as more magic from Katoa created a second try for Olakau'atu.

England are left requiring wins against France and Papua New Guinea in their remaining pool games, plus a favour or two elsewhere, if they are to reach the knockout stages.

England must regroup ahead of facing France in Perth next Saturday, kick-off 7.35am (UK and Ireland time).

articles.summary: PERTH, Australia (AP) — Tonga pulled off a stunner at the Rugby League World Cup on Saturday by beating England 30-12.It was another shock result against a P...
articles.body:
PERTH, Australia (AP) — Tonga pulled off a stunner at the Rugby League World Cup on Saturday by beating England 30-12.

It was another shock result against a Pacific island nation for the English, who were beaten by Samoa in the semifinals on home soil in 2022.

It was the first of third-ranked England's three group-stage games and immediately jeopardizes its progress to the semifinals, with games still to come against France and Papua New Guinea.

Tonga, which had never previously beaten England, is ranked No. 5 in the world and has other group games against Lebanon and Samoa.

Only two of those six teams advance to the last four.

The semifinals of the month-long World Cup are scheduled for Nov. 7 and 8, with the final at Brisbane's Suncorp Stadium on Nov. 15.

articles.summary: England 's men fall to defeat in their Rugby League World Cup opener as Tonga take their chances in Perth.
articles.body:
Tries : Olakau'atu 2, Utoikamanu, Koula Goals : Katoa 3 Penalties : Katoa 4

Four years ago, England were left shocked and shattered by Samoa in the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals.

Now in 2026, Tonga - another Pacific island nation - have done the same with a victory to put England's Australian campaign in immediate jeopardy.

Tonga combined classy attacking play with staunch defence, mixed with a pinch of luck - while being cheered on by a ferociously partisan crowd in Perth - to cause a major upset.

It was expected that Brian McDermott's team - ranked third in the world - would have enough to open their Group B-C campaign with victory over opponents ranked fifth.

But they will now have to pick themselves up for coming group games against France and Papua New Guinea to try to secure a top-two finish in the combined six-team group table and secure a semi-final spot.

England's day came apart amid seemingly endless mistakes, wastefulness and a few dodgy refereeing decisions.

Arguably the turning point came on 22 minutes, when England got to within a few yards of the opposition line but Victor Radley knocked on after an absolute boneshaker from Tonga captain Jason Taumalolo.

The ball was turned over, and the Tongans scored two minutes later. Stefano Utoikamanu streaked through after Isaiya Katoa's superb inside pass cut out George Williams and Kai Pearce-Paul, to the delight of the massed Tongan fans in Perth.

For England, it seemed as if the universe was against them.

The impressive Katoa converted two penalties given following debatable calls. First, Harry Smith was penalised for obstruction when Dallin Watene-Zelezniak ran into him. Then, Herbie Farnworth conceded a sloppy penalty on the verge of half-time when accidentally tripping Watene-Zelezniak off the ball.

England badly needed half-time, and they came out refreshed.

Their first flowing move of the home game led to a try for full-back AJ Brimson after being set up by a sensational driving run from Young, holding off two tacklers over 20 metres.

Waves of England attacks began to crash on the Tongan defence, but Tonga stood firm and benefited from a moment of fortune as Haumole Olakau'atu pounced after his sketchy first grubber kick was kicked on behind the England line.

And with England wobbling, Tonga landed a one-two punch when Tolutau Koula drove over the line.

Young went over in the corner to give England false hope, but in front of their delirious fans Tonga scored their fourth try as Katoa's grubber kick exploited defensive gaps for Olakau'atu to touch down.

In the day's other men's game - also in Group B-C - co-hosts Papua New Guinea defeated Lebanon 42-18.

articles.title: Black Lion 14-39 Ospreys: Welsh side ease to Challenge Cup win in Georgia
articles.summary: Ospreys get off to a winning start in the 2026-27 Challenge Cup, running in seven tries against Black Lion in Georgia.
articles.body:
Tries: Spanderashvili, Giorgadze Cons: Tsirekidze 2

Tries: Evans, Morse, Sutton, Morgan 2, Lloyd, Hire Cons: Creighton 2

Ospreys successfully avoided a Challenge Cup banana skin with a professional bonus-point win against Black Lion in Georgia.

Mark Jones' men scored seven tries at Avchala Stadium in Tbilisi and limited their hosts to two efforts to secure a bonus point.

Ospreys led 22-7 at half-time after tries by all three members of their back row, Gwilym Evans, Morgan Morse and Huw Sutton, plus wing Luke Morgan.

Further scores followed in perfect conditions for running rugby from Morgan, hooker Lewis Lloyd and prop Kian Hire.

It was a win that would have been even more convincing were it not for Lawson Creighton's struggles from the kicking tee.

Swansea celebrate first season win at new St Helen’s

Wales and Ospreys suffer lengthy Hardy injury blow

Black Lion previously upset Scarlets and French pair Vannes and Montauban, while they pushed eventual winners Montpellier hard in 2025-26, but never threatened the Welsh side.

Ospreys will be relieved to return to Swansea for a pair of fixtures after starting their 2026-27 season with away games in Durban, Johannesburg, Newport and Tbilisi.

They will open their revamped St Helen's home with United Rugby Championship (URC) derbies against Dragons and Cardiff before the November international break.

Travel demands have led to Jones and his staff rotating their squad but the changes did not hinder them in Georgia.

Ospreys took command thanks to two unconverted tries inside 12 minutes, with open-side flanker Evans crossing from a well-worked line-out move and number eight Morse finishing powerfully from a five-metre scrum.

Black Lion struck in the 20th minute through scrum-half Giorgi Spanderashvili, who danced through several weak tackles, but the Welsh side regained control with a close-range effort from blind-side Sutton.

Fly-half Creighton's kicking radar was off but the lead was a comfortable 22-7 at half-time thanks to a botched line-out falling kindly to allow Morgan to go over from Lalakai Foketi's offload.

Four-try Dragons beat Perpignan - but without bonus

The Welsh back-row trio starring for Leicester

The second half was a matter of Ospreys protecting their bonus by adding more tries and keeping Black Lion, who offered little other than a formidable scrum, out under new rules in the European competitions .

Morgan acrobatically went over for his second down the left soon after the restart and Reuben Morgan-Williams' fizzed pass put hooker Lloyd in down the other flank.

Replacement prop Hire went over from a yard after centre Owen Watkin's line-break was followed by Lloyd being dragged down just short.

Harri Wilde had a try chalked off by the TMO for offside and the Georgians had the final say through replacement back-row forward Otar Giorgadze from a driving line-out.

Ospreys host Harlequins in December before January fixtures against French opposition at Toulon and at home against Vannes.

Ospreys player of the match Gwilym Evans said:

"We had to start fast because we knew that they pride themselves on their set-piece and physicality.

"We had to match that and wanted to keep the ball in play, moving it about, so we started fast and continued that. We can be happy with the performance."

articles.title: Champions Cup: Sale Sharks 27-47 Glasgow Warriors - visitors record bonus-point win
articles.summary: Glasgow Warriors pull away to record an impressive bonus-point victory over Sale Sharks in the Investec Champions Cup at an emotional CorpAcq Stadium.
articles.body:
Tries: B Curry, Reed 2, Ma'asi-White Cons: Ford 2 Pen: Ford

Tries: Penalty try, Steyn, Dobie, Craig, Darge, Smith, Tuipulotu Cons: Horne 4, Lancaster

Glasgow Warriors pulled away to record an impressive bonus-point victory over Sale Sharks in the Investec Champions Cup on an emotional day at CorpAcq Stadium.

Pre-match tears were shed on the pitch and in the stands during a minute's silence in memory of former Sale lock Hyron Andrews, who died on Friday at the Johannesburg Lions' team hotel before their Champions Cup match at La Rochelle.

The 31-year-old played regularly for Sale last season, and his former side started positively as they sought a memorable performance.

Ben Curry peeled off a maul and sprinted through, much to Glasgow's surprise, before Arron Reed crossed out wide after some sharp handling.

However, a penalty try for a maul infringement sent Gus Warr to the sin-bin, before Tom Roebuck joined him after tripping Warriors captain Kyle Steyn.

After Rory Darge spilled the ball with a try beckoning, Glasgow finally took advantage as Steyn raced down the wing to score.

A wonderful finish by Scotland's Jamie Dobie restored the visitors' lead after George Ford's penalty had put Sale back ahead.

Considered one of the favourites to win the tournament after recording a clean sweep of bonus-point wins in last year's pool stage, Glasgow were stunned by Toulon in the quarter-finals at Scotstoun.

One of those wins came against Sale after Franco Smith's side recovered from 14 points down to win 26-21.

Lock Alex Craig powered over from close range as a similar pattern began to emerge, with Rekeiti Ma'asi-White crossing after sustained pressure to keep Alex Sanderson's side in touch.

A sublime one-handed offload from Joe Carpenter then set up Reed to respond to a Warriors maul try.

However, Smith's side, who will be aiming for a deep run in Europe, crossed through replacement Ollie Smith and Ottavio Tuipulotu to secure an additional bonus point.

A new rule in this year's tournament awards an extra point to teams that score three more tries than their opponents.

The second round of fixtures in the Champions Cup will be played in December, with Glasgow hosting Pau and Sale travelling to Dublin to face Leinster.

Andrews' death 'still really raw to process' - Sanderson

Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson, speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live about the death of former Sharks player Hyron Andrews: "I am really impressed with how the lads have come together, looked after each other and got tighter in the trauma of it.

"It is a good indication of the strength of the squad and the depth of the culture, how much they want to get around each other and get through it together.

"Hyron represents a large portion of the squad, in that he came here underrated and got opportunities to show what he is capable of.

"He forwarded his career, made Manchester his second home, settled with his wife and had another child.

"He left with a lot of good mates and people who consider him as one of their best mates. His impact and what he gave off the field was far more from what he gave on it. It is still really raw to process.

"His two boys are too young to really fathom what is going on but I know the lads close to Hyron have been speaking to his two boys already this morning.

"We will help their family get through it.

"It was not something we looked to use or to weaponise. I'd never want to do that because I think you would kind of be dishonouring him.

"You can ride emotion and some of them wanted to do right by Hyron today. They have to get through it in their own time and way - that is grief.

"Collectively we can grieve together and be there for each other. I imagine they found it hard. I found it hard, trying to come in and be my positive self.

"They didn't really show it with how they started. It shows the pros they are."

Glasgow flanker Rory Darge, speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live: "Sale are a really good side, especially their pack. That was a challenge we set our pack. I thought we did really well at the set piece.

"We will enjoy this as we know how tough Sale are to beat here."

articles.title: Clermont 23-48 Leinster: Seven-try Irish province win Champions Cup pool opener
articles.summary: Leinster launch their quest for an elusive fifth European title with an ultimately comprehensive bonus-point win over Clermont at Stade Marcel-Michelin.
articles.body:
Tries: Jurand, Belaubre Cons: Plummer 2 Pens: Plummer 3

Tries: Furlong, Sheehan 2, Prendergast, penalty try, Conan, T O'Brien Cons: Prendergast 3 Pen: Prendergast

Leinster launched their quest for an elusive fifth European title with an ultimately comprehensive bonus-point win over Clermont at Stade Marcel-Michelin.

Beaten finalists for the fifth time in eight seasons in May, Leinster head coach Leo Cullen loaded his line-up with Ireland internationals and it paid dividends in a seven-try display in their pool one opener.

While Tadhg Furlong and Dan Sheehan scored first-half tries for Leinster, the hosts edged in front before half-time thanks to Joris Jurand's score and 11 points from the boot of fly-half Harry Plummer.

But a superb try from Prendergast - who scored 16 points - within two minutes of the restart set the tone for the second half as the Irish province pulled away with a penalty try awarded before Sheehan struck for the second.

Mathys Belaubre responded for Clermont before Jack Conan and Tommy O'Brien wrapped up a convincing victory for the four-time champions.

Glasgow get bonus-point win at emotion-filled Sale

Bristol beaten by Stormers in Champions Cup opener

Before kick-off, there was a moment's silence in memory of Lions lock Hyron Andrews, who died on Friday aged 31.

Former Sale player Andrews died at the South African team's hotel a day before their Champions Cup match in La Rochelle.

Clermont have struggled in the Top 14 so far this season with four defeats in six, and their fragility was evident early on when Furlong crossed in the ninth minute after Jimmy O'Brien had gone close for Leinster.

While Clermont responded with a couple of Plummer penalties, Sheehan pounced on the tryline to score Leinster's second after the home side's line-out went awry.

Winger Jurand responded for Clermont, who led by a single point at the break after Plummer nailed a long-range penalty.

Following a testing opening period, Prendergast provided Leinster with a moment to savour early in the second half.

The fly-half, who also impressed in last week's United Rugby Championship win over Cardiff, surged through Clermont and picked out Jimmy O'Brien with a kick. The winger controlled the ball with his foot and gathered before picking out the onrushing Prendergast, who ran in under the posts.

Already wounded, Clermont's hopes were further dented when referee Matthew Carley awarded a penalty try with prop Nohem Ez Zahouany sin-binned.

That was followed by Sheehan's second try, and while replacement centre Belaubre touched down in style for the home side, Conan and O'Brien scores in the final quarter of an hour added gloss to the scoreline for the visitors.

'Our thoughts are with the Lions' - Cullen

Leinster head coach Leo Cullen, speaking to Premier Sports: "Lots of really good stuff in the game. Conditions were a bit tricky, greasy ball, particularly in the first half, and Clermont are a physical team.

"It's a great stadium, great crowd. A sad day of course with Hyron Andrews, our thoughts are with the Lions and all the family connected to them. We only played the Lions a couple of weeks ago so [it was] horrific news to wake up to yesterday morning."

Leinster fly-half Sam Prendergast, speaking to Premier Sports: "It's pretty special [to win]. I haven't played here before, it's an unbelievable atmosphere. The place was hopping, it's a surreal experience as it feels like the fans are on top of you.

"I think a lot of it was forward dominance, our pack was excellent, scrum, line-out defence and maul were very good. That got us into the right areas and that meant we."

articles.title: Champions Cup: Stormers 49-12 Bristol Bears - Prem side lose pool-stage opener
articles.summary: Bristol Bears lose their Champions Cup pool-stage opener against Stormers, with Jonathan Roche and Leolin Zas both scoring twice for the South African side.
articles.body:
Tries: Senatla, Zas 2, Roche 2, Gelant, Venter Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu 7

Bristol Bears conceded seven tries as they lost to South African side Stormers in their first pool match of this season's Champions Cup.

Seabelo Senatla raced clear for Stormers' opening score and then showed incredible footwork to control a pass with his boot before offloading to fellow winger Leolin Zas.

Joe Owen powered over in the corner to reply for Bristol but Stormers quickly restored their 14-point advantage with a Jonathan Roche try.

Stormers hooker JJ Kotze was shown a 20-minute red card before the interval for making head-to-head contact in a tackle with Bristol skipper Kieran Marmion.

The Bears had spells of pressure while the hosts were down to 14 players either side of half-time. And in a period when Stormers had just 13 men after Zas had been sin-binned for a high tackle, Bristol finally reduced their deficit as Sol Moody emerged from the back of a maul to touch down.

But any hope of a comeback was short-lived as two Bristol players collided when attempting to claim a high kick and Roche collected the loose ball to score his second.

Replacements Warrick Gelant and Andre-Hugo Venter added further scores late on, as did Zas, to secure a bonus point for Stormers, while South Africa fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu converted all of his side's seven tries.

Bristol, who have won two of their first three Prem games, host Munster in their next Champions Cup fixture on 12 December, before rounding off the pool phase against French clubs Racing 92 and Bordeaux in January.

articles.title: Champions Cup: Munster beat Racing 92 on emotional day of Anthony Foley tributes as Leinster, Glasgow Warriors win big; Saracens, Bath defeated
articles.summary: Munster beat Racing 92 on an emotional anniversary, a decade to the day since their fixture was postponed following the death of coach Anthony Foley in Paris; elsewhere, Leinster and Glasgow Warriors recorded emphatic wins, while Saracens and Bath suffered damaging defeats
articles.body:
The night of Friday October 16, 2016 saw Foley pass away in his sleep the night before Munster were due to face Racing in Paris, with their fixture 10 years on staged at Páirc Uí Chaoimh in Cork.

Munster crossed for five tries in a hard-fought contest, with No 8 Brian Gleeson, wearing 24 as Foley's retired No 8 was once again taken out of circulation, joined on the scoresheet by wing Shay McCarthy, lock Tadhg Beirne, replacement Fineen Wycherley and scrum-half Craig Casey.

Racing responded with three tries of their own through wing Wilfried Hulleu, replacement scrum-half Maxime Machenaud and full-back Geronimo Prisciantelli, denying Munster a bonus-point victory. Under the tournament's new rules, teams must score at least three more tries than their opponents to secure the full five points.

The match came a day after the shocking death of Lions second row Hyron Andrews in France ahead of a Champions Cup fixture in La Rochelle. Emotional tributes were paid to both Andrews and Foley before kick-off.

Glasgow, Leinster post big opening away-day victories | Saracens lose at Connacht

Elsewhere , Glasgow Warriors extended their unbeaten start to the new season by pulling away to claim an impressive 47-27 win at Sale Sharks.

Glasgow's winning score might have looked convincing but they only secured victory in the final 20 minutes after Rekeiti Ma'asi-White had temporarily reduced Sale's deficit to four.

The game looked in the balance until late tries from Rory Darge, Ollie Smith and debutant Otavio Tuipulotu helped Glasgow pull away and wrap up a precious bonus-point win.

Leinster made a flying start to their campaign with an emphatic 48-23 victory away to Clermont Auvergne. Tadhg Furlong, Dan Sheehan (two), Sam Prendergast, Jack Conan and Tommy O'Brien all crossed the line, while a penalty try completed a dominant seven-try display.

Connacht pulled off a stunning 45-36 victory over Saracens in Galway, scoring tries through Cian Prendergast (two), Cathal Forde, Shamus Hurley-Langton, Ciaran Frawley (two) and Caolin Blade.

Bath also endured an evening to forget as they were dispatched at home by Montpellier 32-14 at the Rec in a shock result.

Lions face La Rochelle a day after death of team-mate Andrews

Players stood in silence, with some visibly emotional, as La Rochelle and the Johannesburg-based Lions paid tribute to South African lock Hyron Andrews before Saturday's Champions Cup clash. The 31-year-old died in France on Friday, on the eve of the fixture.

Andrews' No 5 jersey was laid on the pitch as his full name, Hyron Diego Andrews, appeared on the stadium's big screen. Several Lions players were visibly tearful, with team-mates embracing one another and others standing with their heads tilted back and eyes closed during the emotional tribute.

La Rochelle went on to claim a 31-14 victory, with tries from Tevita Ofa (17), Oscar Jegou (30), Davit Niniashvili (39), Tolu Latu (61) and Avakuki Niusalelekitoga (76).

articles.title: Challenge Cup: Zebre 21-40 Ulster - Last season's beaten finalists start with a bonus-point win away in Parma
articles.summary: Ulster run in six tries on their way to a 40-21 bonus-point win over Zebre in Parma to open their European Challenge Cup campaign.
articles.body:
Tries: Licata, Ortombina, Montemauri Cons: Giacomo, Montemauri (2)

Tries: Walker (2), Stockdale, McCann, Lowry, Moloney Cons: Doak (3), Benson (2)

Ulster ran in six tries on their way to a 40-21 bonus-point win over Zebre in Parma to open their European Challenge Cup campaign.

Recent academy graduate Henry Walker shone on his first competitive start for Richie Murphy's side as he scored two tries for the province and showed great promise in the front row against a tenacious Zebre outfit.

Last season's beaten finalists took a 19-0 lead with Jacob Stockdale also crossing in between Walker's first-half double.

Zebre clawed their way back into the contest in the second half but the visitors finished strongly to keep hold of their bonus point.

Ulster's defence was called into action in the opening exchanges of the game after a set-piece play from a Zebre line-out gave the hosts a dangerous chance before the effort was held up.

In a tightly fought opening 10 minutes, Juarno Augusto also saw an effort held up before Walker got over the line for his first senior try for Ulster on the occasion of his first competitive start.

That score seemed to settle Ulster into a rhythm as they marched up the field six minutes later, only for Nathan Doak's finish to be ruled out for a knock-on after a fine passing move.

Stockdale soon rectified the error from his fellow Ireland international as the Ulster full-back finished off a strong team move in the corner to increase the province's lead to 12.

Zebre's afternoon went from bad to worse when Walker dived over to score his second and Ulster's third in the opening half hour.

By the half-time whistle, Ulster held firm and restricted Massimo Brunello's side in their attacking efforts to merely half-chances.

But Zebre came out swinging in the second half as Giovanni Licata rolled down the short side following a scrum to put his side on the scoreboard before Giacomo da Re converted after 43 minutes.

Four minutes later, David McCann marked his first time captaining the side with a try of his own as Ulster quickly restored their 19-point advantage.

With 15 minutes left of what was becoming a tightly-fought second half, Ulster were put under pressure when replacement Jack Murphy was sent to the sin-bin moments after coming on as a replacement.

The hosts, who are bottom of the URC table, took advantage of their numerical superiority just a minute later as they doubled their try tally through Alessandro Ortombina.

Replacement back Mike Lowry continued the high-scoring for Ulster when he finished off a patient but punishing move after he was found on the left wing and produced a finish worthy of the passing build-up.

For the hosts though, the game was far from over, with full-back Giovanni Montemauri scoring a try that temporarily knocked Ulster out of bonus-point range.

Martin Moloney, who replaced McCann for Ulster, however replied within minutes to restore the crucial three-try buffer and seal maximum points from the trip to the Stadio Sergio Lanfranchi.

With the Challenge Cup now parked until December, Ulster face three consecutive away trips back in the URC, starting with a South African double-header against the Bulls and Stormers.
