articles.title: Champions Cup: Connacht 45-36 Saracens - Hosts score seven tries in pool victory
articles.summary: Connacht produce a superb attacking performance to beat Saracens in their opening Champions Cup pool game.
articles.body:
Tries: Prendergast 2, Forde, Hurley-Langton, Frawley 2, Blade Cons: Gilbert 5

Tries: Vaenuku 2, Caluori, Tompkins, Segun, Daly Cons: Farrell 3

Connacht produced a superb attacking performance to beat Saracens in their opening Champions Cup pool game.

Captain Cian Prendergast and fly-half Ciaran Frawley scored two tries apiece as Connacht, third from bottom in the United Rugby Championship table after three games, crossed seven times against the three-time Champions Cup winners at a raucous Dexcom Stadium.

Saracens had the chance to leave with a losing bonus point, but Owen Farrell's conversion attempt after Elliot Daly's late try went wide.

The Prem club had led 12-0 early on with tries from Sione Vaenuku and Noah Caluori.

However, Connacht replied with 19 unanswered points as Prendergast, Cathal Forde and Shamus Hurley-Langton all touched down to put the hosts in front.

Hurley-Langton was sin-binned just before the break and Saracens took advantage almost immediately as Nick Tompkins dummied his way over the line from close range with the clock in the red, meaning an enthralling first half ended 19-19.

Connacht, still with 14 men, scored first in the second period when Bundee Aki set up Prendergast's second, although Saracens' response was swift as Farrell and Daly provided an easy run-in for Rotimi Segun.

Frawley's double and another from replacement Caolin Blade helped Connacht build a 14-point gap, despite centre Vaenuku scoring his second for the visitors, which proved more than enough to see out a hugely impressive victory.

A bonus point eluded Connacht, however, with teams needing to score three or more tries than their opponents to earn one in the pool stage this season.

Elsewhere in Pool Two on Saturday, La Rochelle beat South African side Lions 31-14.

Lions played the match in honour of team-mate Hyron Andrews , who died at the team's hotel on Friday aged 31, with tributes paid to the former Sale Sharks player before kick-off.

articles.title: Hyron Andrews: Lions and Sale Sharks among clubs to pay tribute to late South African lock
articles.summary: Lions and Sale Sharks are among the clubs to pay tribute to Hyron Andrews at their matches on Saturday, following the South African's death aged 31.
articles.body:
Lions and Sale Sharks were among the clubs to pay tribute to Hyron Andrews at their matches on Saturday, following the South African's death aged 31.

Former Sale lock Andrews died at the Lions' team hotel on Friday, a day before their Champions Cup pool game against La Rochelle in France.

The Lions, who said they would fulfil the fixture in Andrews' honour, lost 31-14.

Asked before the match why the Lions had chosen to play, head coach Ivan van Rooyen said: "It's been a tough 24 hours and we've decided to celebrate Hyron, show respect to his wife and his children, and celebrate life. It gets taken away so quickly.

"We've had hundreds and thousands of messages from all over the world.

"It's not about winning or losing today. It's not about rugby.

"We want to show the respect to Hyron, who was an unbelievable guy, an unbelievable player, a world-class dad and a world-class husband.

"Us arriving for the game shows how much he means to us and how much it means to everyone."

There was prolonged applause from La Rochelle supporters as the Lions players entered the field, and also after the minute's silence that was observed before kick-off.

Both sides wore black armbands and several players shed tears during the period of silence, while Andrews' number five jersey was laid out on the turf in front of the Lions' team.

Three South African players in La Rochelle's squad - Dillyn Leyds, David Kriel and Salmaan Moerat - then presented a commemorative jersey to their opponents.

There were pre-match tributes before all of this weekend's Champions Cup and Challenge Cup fixtures, including at Andrews' former club Sale.

Andrews spent just over two years with the Prem club before departing at the end of last season and returning to his native South Africa.

Speaking after their 47-27 loss to Glasgow Warriors, Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson told BBC Radio 5 Live: "I am really impressed with how the lads have come together, looked after each other and got tighter in the trauma of it.

"It is a good indication of the strength of the squad and the depth of the culture, how much they want to get around each other and get through it together.

"Hyron represents a large portion of the squad, in that he came here under-rated and got opportunities to show what he is capable of.

"He forwarded his career, made Manchester his second home, settled with his wife and had another child.

"He left with a lot of good mates and people who consider him as one of their best mates. His impact and what he gave off the field was far more from what he gave on it. It is still really raw to process.

"His two boys are too young to really fathom what is going on but I know the lads close to Hyron have been speaking to his two boys already this morning.

"We will help their family get through it."

articles.title: Champions Cup: Bath 14-32 Montpellier - French side excel in second half to win
articles.summary: Montpellier score 22 second-half points without reply to beat Bath on the opening weekend of the Champions Cup.
articles.body:
Tries: Hogg, Taofifenua 2, Becognee Cons: Hastings 3 Pens: Hastings 2

Montpellier earned an impressive victory at Bath, rounding off a disappointing Saturday for English clubs in the Champions Cup.

After Gloucester's high-scoring draw against holders Bordeaux on Friday, Bath joined Sale, Bristol and Saracens in losing their opening pool fixture.

Leicester, Exeter and Northampton are all in action on Sunday.

Bath had scored at least 33 points in each of their first three Prem games this season but failed to reach those heights in attack during their Pool Four opener at The Rec.

The hosts had a try disallowed in both halves, while Joe Cokanasiga failed to cleanly gather a pass with the tryline beckoning when they led 14-10 early in the second period.

Bath were punished by Donovan Taofifenua's second-half double and an Alex Becognee try for last season's Challenge Cup winners Montpellier, who scored 22 points without reply after half-time.

Recap: Saturday's Champions Cup action as it happened

Bath had already had a Max Ojomoh try ruled out for a knock-on when Montpellier's former Scotland full-back Stuart Hogg raced in for the first points of the match.

The hosts would soon be on the scoreboard themselves as England centre Ollie Lawrence barged over in the corner, before number eight Arthur Green brilliantly sidestepped past a defender to put the Prem club in front.

Montpellier, beaten Top 14 finalists last season, kept in touch with an Adam Hastings penalty before the interval.

Cokanasiga's missed opportunity proved costly almost immediately as winger Taofifenua dived over in the corner to make it 15-14 in the French side's favour.

Hastings added a further three points from the tee and after an excellent defensive spell by the visitors, Taofifenua intercepted a Finn Russell pass on halfway and sped away from the chasing Bath defenders to score his second.

Josh Bayliss' try for Bath did not stand because of an infringement earlier in the move, and Becognee burrowed over from close range in the final few minutes for Montpellier to make the win safe.

Bath's remaining pool fixtures are against Cardiff, South African side Bulls and Stade Francais.

The latter two of those teams met earlier on Saturday, with Bulls scoring eight tries in a convincing 56-20 victory against their French opponents.

Cheswill Jooste ended with a hat-trick, having opened the scoring inside 20 seconds, in a bonus-point win.
